correctness.rationale: Direct double-counting proves at least six red and blue points, and classifies every feasible six-point class as six intersections of a four-line general-position frame. 5616 ordered frames/24 give 234 such classes; complements give 234 more. Each frame permits exactly three red additions, and the 234-frame disjointness graph is its exact bipartite-half quotient. The 24-element frame stabilizer is neighbor-transitive, as exhaustively independently verified. Separate affine and vector projective-plane constructions check all 8192 point bicolorings, every possible one-point flip, all 234 graph vertices, all BFS distance distributions and girths, and all 5616 projectivities. With the published complete 234-order symmetric-cubic census, this identifies F234B and its F468 double cover. No finite-sample inference to an infinite-family theorem is made.

value.rationale: The natural reconfiguration question for line-bichromatic point colorings has a complete structural solution: precisely 468 labeled feasible assignments, every one with three legal single-point recolorings, mutual reachability and sharp diameter 13. The projective-frame derivation explains this behavior and establishes a concrete connection to a rare 5-arc-transitive graph. A graph name/count alone does not answer the exact feasible-recoloring operation or its geometric meaning. Despite being finite, the structural classification is a motivated, complete natural invariant.
